title: Barrett’s oesophagus and oesophageal adenocarcinoma

brief.scenario: You are a core surgical trainee at the oesophago-gastric MDT teaching assessment. The examiner will hand you a written endoscopy and histology report. Report A: 61-year-old with Barrett’s segment C2M4 and a 12-mm visible distal-oesophageal nodule. Targeted biopsies: high-grade dysplasia (HGD), confirmed by two gastrointestinal pathologists. CT has not yet been performed.
brief.task: Interpret it, outline management and respond to new information. No photograph is required.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Differentiate dysplasia from intramucosal and invasive adenocarcinoma; choose the treatment according to confirmed histology, not appearance alone.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Confusing high-grade dysplasia with invasive stage, or treating visible lesions with ablation before histological resection.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Check the visible lesion and confirmed pathology.

flow: Confirm histological diagnosis, lesion visibility and whether pathology review is complete.
Separate flat dysplasia from visible lesions: resect the visible lesion first.
Interpret resection histology and propose treatment for favourable T1a cancer.
Discuss staging when disease is beyond early T1a, with specialist MDT.
Explain surveillance, pathology uncertainty and safety-netting without overpromising.

grid.label: Report interpretation
grid.borderline: Recognises dysplasia but cannot distinguish nodule from flat mucosa.
grid.pass: Identifies visible lesion and pathologist-confirmed HGD.
grid.high: Explains why endoscopic resection gives histological staging as well as treatment.

grid.label: Risk communication
grid.borderline: States cancer risk vaguely without explaining uncertainty.
grid.pass: Explains HGD is serious and needs specialist treatment.
grid.high: Separates premalignant dysplasia from subsequent confirmed invasive cancer.

grid.label: Visible lesion management
grid.fail: Proposes ablation alone of an unresected nodule.
grid.borderline: Suggests ablation before clarifying visible lesion histology.
grid.pass: Recommends endoscopic resection first for visible HGD lesion.
grid.high: Plans MDT/pathology review of depth and margins before further treatment.

grid.label: Residual Barrett’s
grid.borderline: Mentions follow-up but not residual segment treatment.
grid.pass: Recommends ablation of residual Barrett’s after resecting HGD.
grid.high: Coordinates specialist ablation and surveillance with the patient’s fitness/preferences.

grid.label: T1a pathology
grid.fail: Treats T1a as automatically requiring oesophagectomy.
grid.borderline: Identifies early cancer but cannot interpret favourable features.
grid.pass: Offers endoscopic resection first line for T1a cancer.
grid.high: Explains how histology and patient context drive further MDT discussion.

grid.label: Stage escalation
grid.fail: Uses PET-CT routinely for the initial T1a lesion.
grid.pass: For radical-treatment non-T1a disease, recommends whole-body CT followed by PET-CT.
grid.high: Uses EUS selectively only when it changes management; explains exceptions.

grid.label: MDT decisions
grid.borderline: Mentions MDT only after proposing definitive treatment.
grid.pass: Refers confirmed cancer and uncertain margins to specialist OG MDT.
grid.high: Asks for expert pathology, endoscopy and surgical assessment together.

grid.label: Consent and expectations
grid.pass: Discusses ongoing endoscopic surveillance and possibility of further treatment.
grid.high: Explains residual/metachronous risk and shared decision-making clearly.

grid.label: Curveball response
grid.fail: Continues T1a pathway after the new T2 report.
grid.borderline: Notices T2 but forgets PET-CT/MDT implications.
grid.pass: Switches to radical-treatment staging and specialist MDT for T2 disease.
grid.high: Recognises PET-CT after CT and only uses EUS if it changes treatment.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What do you make of the 12-mm nodule and HGD?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: High-grade dysplasia means the patient definitely has deep invasive cancer. I would arrange an operation immediately.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Are you certain of invasion from the biopsy?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, I think HGD always means invasive cancer.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No, I would simply ablate the visible lump and avoid taking more tissue.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Suppose the nodule is resected and shows HGD only. What about the rest of the C2M4 segment?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Nothing more is needed once the nodule is out; the rest of the Barrett’s can be left alone.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Resection elsewhere instead shows favourable T1a disease.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: T1a still mandates oesophagectomy in everybody, regardless of fitness or pathology.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you stage this T1a lesion?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would request PET-CT, as I would for every oesophageal cancer.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would decide myself and list the patient for oesophagectomy; the MDT does not need to see it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: None once the lump is treated.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Now the lesion is T2 and suitable for radical therapy.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It is basically identical to T1a, so I would not stage it further or discuss it with the MDT.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Read Report A. What is most important?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: There is confirmed high-grade dysplasia in Barrett’s oesophagus, and importantly a visible 12-mm nodule. I would verify the endoscopy description and expert histology review.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not on these biopsies. HGD is a high-risk premalignant finding; sampling cannot fully characterise the visible lesion, so we must not equate the biopsy result with the final stage.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would arrange specialist endoscopic resection of the visible lesion as first-line treatment and to establish accurate histological stage, rather than simply ablating the nodule.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: After resection, I would offer endoscopic ablation of residual Barrett’s and organise endoscopic follow-up through a specialist service.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The resection shows a well differentiated T1a adenocarcinoma, clear deep margin and no lymphovascular invasion.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That is intramucosal early cancer with favourable reported features. Endoscopic resection is first-line for T1a oesophageal adenocarcinoma, with ablation of residual Barrett’s and specialist follow-up.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Would you send the patient straight for oesophagectomy?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No. I would discuss suitability of endoscopic treatment and oesophagectomy with the patient in the specialist OG team, taking final pathology and individual factors into account.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Can you promise that treatment ends all future risk?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No. Treatment is effective but does not remove the need for follow-up. I would explain that further endoscopy or therapy may be needed.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: New case: histology now says T2 cancer and radical treatment appears possible. What changes?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This is not an uncomplicated T1a endoscopic case. After diagnostic endoscopy and whole-body CT, the person suitable for radical therapy should have FDG PET-CT; EUS only if it would guide management. The specialist MDT decides treatment.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Would you insist on EUS merely to differentiate T2 from T3?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No. NICE advises against EUS solely for that distinction. I would explain why the test is needed if ordering it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The two separate questions are whether the visible lesion contains invasive carcinoma and how much abnormal Barrett’s mucosa remains. Biopsy-confirmed HGD alone does not provide full invasion depth. I would check the Prague length and lesion description, and confirm expert GI pathology review.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Specialist endoscopic resection of the 12-mm visible nodule; I would not ablate it in situ because histology from resection is essential for staging and margin assessment.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you phrase this to the patient?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would explain that the biopsies show a serious change that can precede cancer, and that removal of the visible area both treats it and tells us more precisely whether cancer is present. I would avoid promising the biopsy has excluded invasion.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The final specimen is T1a, well differentiated, no lymphovascular invasion and clear deep margin.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That confirms intramucosal adenocarcinoma. In a suitable patient, NICE recommends endoscopic resection first line for T1a disease. I would review complete histology and risk features with the specialist MDT before confirming next steps.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What do you do with C2M4 remaining Barrett’s mucosa?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Offer endoscopic ablation after lesion resection, then a planned endoscopic follow-up programme. I would clarify the endoscopist’s eradication plan and document what has actually been treated.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The patient says, “So this is cured and I never need another scope?”

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would say the early cancer is often treatable endoscopically, but future Barrett’s-related change remains possible. Follow-up is a central part of care, and we should discuss its burden and benefits.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No. Treatment options and patient fitness must be evaluated in a specialist OG meeting, particularly if adverse histological factors, incomplete resection, or more advanced disease emerge.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Now I replace the case with a confirmed T2 oesophageal cancer suitable for radical treatment.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would stop using the T1a-only pathway. After diagnostic endoscopy and whole-body CT, PET-CT should be offered for radical-treatment candidates other than T1a. An EUS has value only if it changes management, not simply to label T2 versus T3.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What needs to happen before the treatment plan is final?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Specialist OG MDT discussion with staging, nutritional and fitness assessment, and a patient-centred discussion of curative options. I would not choose a single operation based on this snippet.

failures.move: Ablating a visible HGD lesion without first obtaining the indicated resection histology
Insisting on oesophagectomy for every favourable T1a lesion without consideration of endoscopic resection
failures.consequence: exposes patients to potentially unnecessary major surgery.

failures.move: Treating T2 oesophageal cancer as T1a and bypassing appropriate staging

recovery.when: If you have treated the biopsy as the final stage
recovery.line: I have treated the biopsy as the final stage. Let me correct that: this visible lesion needs resection histology before deciding the pathway.

recovery.when: The new report changes the stage to T2
recovery.line: The new report changes the stage to T2; I will leave the early-endoscopic pathway and arrange full staging through the specialist MDT.

knowledge.fact: A visible lesion with HGD should undergo endoscopic resection first.
Residual Barrett’s after HGD resection should be ablated.
T1a adenocarcinoma should have endoscopic resection first line.
Residual Barrett’s after T1a resection should receive ablation.
PET-CT for radical candidates except T1a; EUS only if management is changed.
Confirmed cancer management is assessed by a specialist OG MDT.

recall.think: Identify the visible lesion and confirm histology, not just the word “Barrett’s”.
recall.say: “We need tissue from the nodule before we can define its depth.”
do: Resect visible HGD/T1a lesion; plan residual Barrett’s ablation where indicated.

numbers.meaning: no stand-alone numeric threshold for PET-CT beyond the stage exception.

recall.trap: Do not ablate a visible nodule without resection/staging.
recall.finish: Agree MDT management and endoscopic follow-up.

sources.name: NICE. Barrett’s oesophagus and stage 1 oesophageal adenocarcinoma: monitoring and management. NG231
NICE. Oesophago-gastric cancer: assessment and management in adults. NG83

partner.opening: Please review Report A and tell me the diagnosis and next step.

reveals.trigger: Provide resection result only when asked about subsequent histology or after initial management
reveals.finding: endoscopic resection histology reveals well differentiated intramucosal T1a adenocarcinoma, clear deep margin, no lymphovascular invasion.
a different patient has biopsy-proven T2 oesophageal adenocarcinoma suitable for radical therapy.
Do not disclose adverse histology absent from the supplied written reports.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Offers endoscopic resection first line for T1a cancer.
